text:
sarah: Quick check-in about partner Terraform modules for cloud marketplaces. Want a lightweight CI gate so marketplace modules meet minimal security, packaging, and operator expectations before listing. Thinking: lint + security scan + tiny smoke deploy that can be toggled. Thoughts?

alex: I'm for a toggle. Many partners will open PRs from forks; need a strict lint path that runs without creds. Do all static checks first, only run terratest/acceptance if maintainer flips a label.

maria: Agree. Propose two gates: "static" and "integration". Static = terraform fmt/validate, tflint, checkov, docs present. Integration = small create/destroy test against dev account, limited to a few resource types.

dan: For integration tests keep them <8m and single-region to avoid flakiness. Also include a mock provider mode for local devs and forks so authors get feedback without secrets.

sarah: Good. Also want a module interface contract: inputs = {region, environment (dev/prod), instance_size, tags}, outputs = {endpoint, module_id, iam_role_arn}. Document in MODULE_INTERFACE.md.

alex: Packaging notes: each release must include a registry metadata file (redwood_registry.yml) with version, supported clouds, cost-estimate and hashing for artifacts. Release workflow should produce a .tar.gz with examples/ and tests/ included.

maria: Cost-estimates are important. Add an examples/ COSTS.md that lists approximate hourly resource costs in each cloud region (use small instance types). Also include a quota note for CI run so partners don't get billed unexpectedly.

dan: Security: require checkov baseline and a short manual review step for any resources exposing internet-facing endpoints. Add a tag `partner:security-reviewed` before we publish.

sarah: I'll draft a CONTRIBUTING.md with the checklists and a PR template. For CI idea, sample workflow:
```yaml
name: partner-module-ci
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  static:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: terraform fmt + validate
        run: |
          terraform fmt -check
          terraform init -backend=false
          terraform validate
      - name: tflint
        run: tflint --module
      - name: checkov
        run: checkov -d .
  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: static
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'run-integration')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup TF
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
        with:
          terraform_version: '1.4.6'
      - name: run terratest (short)
        run: go test ./tests -run TestQuick -timeout 8m
```

alex: Nice. A couple of operational asks: 1) automated cleanup hooks so partial failures don't leave stray resources, 2) provider version pins in provider.tf and examples to avoid drift.

maria: Also add a small example that wires module outputs into a Redwood marketplace deployment manifest so partners understand expected output keys. That reduces integration back-and-forth.

dan: For partner onboarding flow: PR -> static checks -> partner answers a short security questionnaire (forms link) -> once answered, maintainer can add label to run integration -> if integration passes, release workflow can be triggered. Automate changelog generation and semver tagging.
\sarah: I'll spin up a seed repo: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-terraform-shared with: templates/, MODULE_INTERFACE.md, examples/, .github/workflows/partner-module-ci.yml, and a sample module. Will include a governance doc for reviewers.

ci-bot: Created PART-1278: "Partner Terraform CI baseline + release metadata" (assignee: sarah).

alex: Action items: Alex -> create registry metadata schema + sample redwood_registry.yml. Maria -> authorship doc + examples wiring. Dan -> terratest TestQuick example + cleanup wrapper. Sarah -> seed repo + CONTRIBUTING.md + PR template.

maria: I'll coordinate a pilot with one AWS partner next Tuesday. Will take the module interface and cost template.

sarah: Thanks team. Aim to have initial artifacts by Friday EOD. If anyone wants a starter module, I can drop a skeleton under templates/seed-small-instance. :rocket:
